summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 9.2.24 (RHEL7 base channel) streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2, and node3 (standbys). Verified live streaming replication, then exercised a full primary-loss failover: stopped node1, promoted node2 to writable primary with zero committed-data loss, repointed node3 to follow node2 (copying the new timeline history file since PG 9.2 can't fetch it over the replication stream), and rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via pg_basebackup. Final topology: node2 = writable primary, node1 and node3 = streaming standbys, all data (4 rows in repl_check) consistent across all three. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), confirming boot_id change and full replication/data recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 9.2.24 server/contrib on node1, node2, node3 from the RHEL7 base channel (PGDG repos were dead-end due to missing libzstd/EPEL access on RHEL7)
Initialized primary DB on node1; configured wal_level=hot_standby, max_wal_senders, wal_keep_segments, hot_standby=on; opened firewalld port 5432
Created 'replicator' REPLICATION LOGIN role on node1 with a password generated on-node via openssl, passed to other nodes only via secret_env
Created pg_hba.conf entries permitting replication + client connections from all three node IPs
Built node2 and node3 as standbys via pg_basebackup from node1, with recovery.conf (standby_mode, primary_conninfo, trigger_file, recovery_target_timeline=latest)
Verified live streaming replication and pg_stat_replication on node1 with two connected standbys; confirmed inserted rows replicate to both standbys
Simulated primary loss: stopped postgresql on node1; promoted node2 via pg_ctl promote; verified zero data loss and write capability on node2

Repointed node3 to follow node2: copied 00000002.history via scp (cluster SSH key) since PG 9.2 walreceiver can't fetch timeline history over streaming replication; updated node3 recovery.conf and restarted; confirmed reconnection and full data
Rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2: wiped its data dir, pg_basebackup from node2, recovery.conf pointed at node2, started and confirmed streaming reconnection with full data
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime baseline plus healthy replication/data proof on all three nodes
Enabled postgresql.service for boot persistence on all three nodes (previously disabled, so the standby DB engine would not have restarted automatically)

Rebooted node1, then node3, then node2 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling until exec returned, confirming changed boot_id, and verifying full data/replication recovery after each before moving to the next node

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication set up node1(primary)->node2,node3(standbys), baseline live-write propagation verified
evidence.summary: node1 primary running PG9.2 with replicator role and table repl_check; pg_stat_replication shows node2 and node3 streaming; a live INSERT on node1 appeared on both standbys.

evidence.requirement: Primary loss triggers standby promotion to writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: 3rd committed row confirmed replicated to both standbys before primary (node1) was stopped; node2 promoted (pg_is_in_recovery=f) with all 3 pre-failover rows intact plus a new post-promotion write, proving zero data loss and restored writability.

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary rejoins as standby of whichever node is primary; surviving standby also re-follows the new primary
evidence.summary: node3 repointed to node2 and streaming (state=streaming, all 4 rows present); node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2 and streaming as its standby with all 4 rows; node2 pg_stat_replication shows both node1 and node3 connected.

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node1 baseline boot_id / healthy standby state before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id 809708f3... prior to restart (post rejoin as standby of node2).

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node1 restart acknowledged, boot_id changed, standby recovery verified
evidence.summary: boot_id changed to 9b39c715...; postgresql enabled+started, log shows 'streaming replication successfully connected to primary'; repl_check shows all 4 rows and pg_is_in_recovery=t.

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node3 baseline boot_id / healthy standby state before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node3 boot_id ef457a88... prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node3 restart acknowledged, boot_id changed, standby recovery verified
evidence.summary: reboot ack + disconnect observed; boot_id changed to 771a49c3...; postgresql auto-started (enabled) and reconnected via streaming replication; repl_check shows all 4 rows, pg_is_in_recovery=t.

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node2 (primary) baseline boot_id / healthy primary state before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id 192f6cab... prior to restart (node2 was the active writable primary).

evidence.requirement: Node-restart protocol: node2 restart acknowledged, boot_id changed, primary + cluster-wide recovery verified last
evidence.summary: reboot ack + disconnect observed; boot_id changed to 7813e57c...; postgresql active; pg_is_in_recovery=f (still writable primary), all 4 rows intact, and pg_stat_replication shows node1 and node3 both reconnected streaming, confirming full cluster quorum/health restored after the final node restart.
